The 1988–89 season was [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s 87th season in existence and the club's 58th consecutive season in the top flight of Spanish football. As of the 2025–26 season, this was the most recent in which the club won a domestic [[Double (association football)|double]] of [[La Liga]] and [[Copa del Rey]] and thus the domestic [[Treble (association football)|treble]] if also counting the [[Supercopa de España]].

== Season ==
Real Madrid finished the season as champions for the fourth consecutive season,<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|title=Sólo siete equipos repitieron título de Liga esta temporada en el fútbol europeo|url=https://www.abc.es/archivo/periodicos/abc-sevilla-19890620-60.html|language=es|date=20 June 1989}}</ref> five points ahead of the runners-up [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]. Real Madrid defeated [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] 3–0 on 10 June, becoming champions with two rounds remaining in the season.<ref>{{cite news|work=[[El País]]|title=El Madrid debe ganar al Español para ser campeón|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1989/06/11/deportes/613519207_850215.html|language=es|date=11 June 1989}}</ref> This was its 24th title in history. Real Madrid also won the Copa del Rey and Supercopa, the first time the club accomplished a domestic treble.<ref>{{cite news|publisher=ABC|title=El Real Madrid lo copa todo|url=https://www.abc.es/archivo/periodicos/abc-madrid-19890701-1.html|language=es|date=1 July 1989}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|newspaper=[[AS (newspaper)|AS]]|title=Objetivo triplete|url=https://as.com/futbol/2022/01/22/copa_del_rey/1642884052_489267.html|language=es|date=22 January 2022}}</ref>
